material_note: proteinaceous, often with silica scales taken from euglyphid prey
pore_type_position: small lateral pores, usually present, ca. 1/3 of the way from pseudostome to fundus; often hard to see
keel_note: genus reached by the 'keel absent' branch of the key
neck_note: sides taper from the widest point (ca. 2/3 from the pseudostome) to the aperture; A. longicollis has a long neck
aperture_narrow_ref: K25 p.37-38 (deep notch in profile view)
outline_note: A. kivuense often laterally curved in broad view (L/B 2.4-2.7)
fundus_note: profile: elongated elliptical with a slightly pointed end (A. longicollis)
size_note: A. kivuense 49-64, A. militaris 50-82, A. longicollis 120-140
diagnostic_vs: Nebela, Longinebela: fan-shaped strongly curved pseudostome with a flare in broad view and a deep notch in profile

material_note: almost transparent organic test, smooth or slightly granulose; some populations with small oval recycled plates in organic cement
pore_type_position: 1-3 small lateral pores on each side of the neck, often hard to see in LM
neck_note: well-developed neck separated from the body by two lateral indentations (constriction lateral only, not circular)
aperture_margin_note: thick organic rim (Tierra del Fuego material)
diagnostic_vs: Apodera vas, Padaungiella lageniformis: indentation on either side of the neck base (lateral only, not a circular constriction)

keel_note: A. angatakere: hollow keel round the posterior body; other species without keel
neck_note: deep circular constriction around the entire base of the neck; neck sides more or less convex (straight to slightly concave with a basal bulge in A. angatakere); neck curved in A. crenata
aperture_margin_note: crenate pseudostome margin in A. crenata (unusual for the family); organic rim otherwise
compression_ref: K25 p.48 (compressed posterior body; constriction oval in frontal view)
outline_note: two distinct parts: subcircular, oval or ellipsoidal body and a neck
size_note: A. crenata ca. 93-120, A. vas 130-170 (reported 90-234), A. wellingtonia 185-220, A. angatakere 186-226
diagnostic_vs: Alocodera, Padaungiella, Certesella, Hyalosphenia elegans: deep circular constriction at the neck base; A. angatakere vs Padaungiella kenyana (both with hollow keel): constriction

material_note: recycled euglyphid plates in organic cement, often covered by a thick organic layer (smooth look)
pore_type_position: two large pores (2-5 um) in lateral depressions on the broad side near the margin, joined by internal tubes, ca. 2/3 from fundus to pseudostome (neck base); some species also small lateral pores ca. 10 um towards the aperture
keel_note: absent (C. martiali), narrow (C. certesi), short hollow keel at the neck base (C. australis)
horns_note: two small triangular expansions where the lateral pores lie (some species)
neck_note: from slightly to well differentiated; internal conical teeth in the neck seen as dots in LM
aperture_margin_note: thick organic lip; row of internal teeth parallel to the pseudostome edge (punctuations)
size_note: C. certesi 80-157; C. martiali 147-238; largest species 199.5-277.5
diagnostic_vs: Porosia: internal neck teeth (dots in LM) and a more elongated flask shape; Apodera: no circular constriction

material_note: circular to elongated plates most likely recycled from euglyphid prey
keel_note: description: horns free or joined to the body by a lateral hollow keel, sometimes surrounding the fundus (horseshoe); key: a flat extension similar to the Planocarina keel
horns_note: two lateral hollow conical horns, pointing towards the fundus, starting ca. 1/3 of the way from pseudostome to fundus
neck_note: lateral margins tapering towards the aperture
size_note: 'four large species (L = 195-270 um)'; C. ansata (195) 220-264 (270) incl. horns; C. equicalceus 252-260; C. jiuhuensis 176-229 (n = 31)
diagnostic_vs: Planocarina, Gibbocarina: pair of lateral hollow horns

material_note: circular to elongated plates likely recycled from euglyphid prey
pore_type_position: two small lateral pores, one per side, often hard to see (G. gracilis)
keel_note: hollow tuberous keel surrounding the entire fundus; internal margin of the keel irregular (G. gracilis) or smooth (G. galeata)
neck_note: sides gradually taper towards the pseudostome
outline_note: tuberous keel gives a wavy outline
fundus_note: rounded, sometimes slightly pointed; pointed tip (keel) in profile
diagnostic_vs: Planocarina: keel hollow, not flat (seen in profile); Mrabella: round, not square plates; Longinebela: keel and wavy outline

material_note: entirely organic, transparent, no visible structure in LM; H. punctata made of small organic hexagonal prisms
pore_type_position: H. papilio: 2 (up to 12) pores on the lateral margin of the posterior end; H. elegans: 2 small pores on the neck; several species without pores
keel_note: H. ligata: keel visible only in profile; H. ovalis: narrow hollow keel
neck_note: wedge-shaped without neck (H. papilio) to flask-shaped with a clear neck (H. elegans)
aperture_margin_note: rim thickened inwards or not (key character at species level)
aperture_narrow_ref: K25 p.93-102 (oval/elliptical in frontal view; notched in profile in several species)
compression_ref: K25 p.80 (except H. savoiei, circular cross-section)
outline_note: rounded, ovoid, elongated elliptical, wedge-shaped or lageniform
fundus_note: all species except one with a pointed posterior end
size_note: H. minuta-like small species 26-43; H. gigantea 204-272
diagnostic_vs: all plated genera: transparent organic test without visible plates in LM; Nebela species whose plates are hidden under thick organic cement look homogeneous too

material_note: circular to elongated recycled euglyphid plates; L. speciosa also Quadrulella plates and diatoms; L. golemanskyi globular hollow siliceous plates
pore_type_position: L. speciosa: two readily visible lateral pores; L. tubulosa: small, hard to see; L. ampulla, L. golemanskyi: none
keel_note: differs from Planocarina and Gibbocarina by the absence of a keel
horns_note: lateral triangular bumps at the pores in the N. penardiana group (key)
neck_note: 'distinct (sometimes short) neck' in the description, but the key places the genus among tests whose neck tapers and is never clearly separated from the body
aperture_margin_note: thin to thick collar of organic cement
compression_ref: K25 p.105 (except L. golemanskyi: circular section)
outline_note: lateral margins straight or wavy (L. meisterfeldi)
fundus_note: L. tubulosa: pointed fundus in profile
diagnostic_vs: Nebela: elongated-piriform, not ovoid/piriform; Planocarina: no flat keel; Gibbocarina: no hollow keel or wavy outline; Alabasta: less curved pseudostome. No single diagnostic character

material_note: quadrangular plates like Quadrulella; self-secreted or recycled (kleptosquamy) unresolved; M. plicata with small round or angular plates between the squares
pore_type_position: two lateral pores at the neck-body junction / where the keel starts
keel_note: lateral margins compressed, giving a thick, wide hollow keel
horns_note: test can be laterally swollen just above the neck-body junction
neck_note: sides gradually tapering towards the pseudostome or neck
diagnostic_vs: Quadrulella: hollow keel (Q. alata has a flat keel); Gibbocarina: square plates, similar shape and hollow keel

material_note: circular to elongated plates recycled from euglyphid prey, sometimes diatom fragments; may be hidden under thick organic cement (homogeneous look); N. dydevallei irregular polygonal plates
pore_type_position: small lateral pores in many species, number variable, often hard to see; N. aliciae, N. orbicularis two lateral pores
keel_note: N. carinatella: short keel near the pseudostome; N. aliciae, N. orbicularis: hollow keel
horns_note: 'rarely with a keel or other lateral expansions'
neck_note: N. acolla without neck; most species a very short neck
diagnostic_vs: Longinebela: ovoid/piriform vs elongated-piriform; Alabasta: pseudostome not fan-shaped nor notched; keeled Nebela species vs Planocarina/Gibbocarina; Argynnia/Physochila: organic rim at the aperture

material_note: circular to elongated plates from small euglyphids; P. nebeloides uses mineral particles (agglutinated look)
neck_note: elongated neck with slightly convex margins, no circular constriction at its base
aperture_margin_note: organic rim from nearly absent to thick
aperture_narrow_ref: K25 p.140 (key 1: circular or ovoid in frontal view)
compression_ref: K25 p.139 (except P. nebeloides, P. pulcherrima: circular section)
fundus_note: key uses the posterior end in profile: pointed (or hollow keel) vs rounded
size_note: P. tubulata-like small species 55-74; P. kenyana 191-212
diagnostic_vs: Apodera: no circular constriction at the neck base; Alocodera: no lateral indentations; Certesella: no large pores or neck teeth; Quadrulella lageniformis: round, not square plates

material_note: circular to elongated plates most likely recycled from euglyphid prey
pore_type_position: small lateral pores, one per side, ca. 1/3 of the way from pseudostome to fundus (usually visible)
keel_note: flat keel round the whole fundus or only the sides; keel outline straight or serrated (wavy in P. maxima)
fundus_note: P. spumosa: pointed fundus in profile
diagnostic_vs: Gibbocarina: keel flat, not hollow (profile view); Cornutheca: no horns; Porosia paracarinata: no large invaginated pores; Nebela carinatella: keel round the fundus, not a short anterior keel

material_note: circular or elliptical plates, often covered by a thick layer of organic cement
pore_type_position: two lateral depressions with large invaginated pores joined by tubes crossing the test, ca. 2/3 from fundus to pseudostome; small lateral pores just anterior (profile)
keel_note: P. bigibbosa no keel; P. paracarinata flat keel
neck_note: less elongated than Certesella; 'absence of neck' cited as distinctive
diagnostic_vs: Certesella: no internal neck teeth, more piriform; Planocarina/Nebela: large invaginated pores in depressions

pore_type_position: Q. elegans: two lateral pores ca. 1/4 of the way from pseudostome to fundus; most species none visible in LM
keel_note: Q. alata: flat keel 5-10 um (most visible in profile)
neck_note: with or without distinct neck (Q. longicollis, Q. lageniformis long neck)
aperture_margin_note: organic rim, tiny to well developed
diagnostic_vs: Mrabella: no hollow keel; Hyalosphenia punctata: square siliceous plates, not organic hexagons; Padaungiella lageniformis vs Q. lageniformis: plate shape, size
